_comment: Lantern charge and knockdown/revive tuning. Charge existed in the scaffold but never drained, which made the solo Anchor Revive free - it is paid for with 'a full lantern charge', and a charge that never depletes costs nothing. Values are placeholders for Chris.

charge._note: 0 means the lantern never runs out. Chris's call, 2026-10-20: "i don't think the lantern should ever run out of light, its kind of a hurt to run out and then be all like running around like that. the risk is always having it on." The cost of light is the Storm Charge it pours into the meter, not a fuel gauge. Was 150, which made a dry lantern a second failure state on top of the storm - you were punished for having used the thing the game is named after.
charge._anchorRevivePrice: RESOLVED, Chris's call 2026-10-20: once per run is the price. The Anchor Revive costs chargesPerRun (1) and a permanent Storm Charge spike of 120, and nothing else. The handoff sentence pricing it at 'a full lantern charge' is now stale and wants rewriting - the mechanic is right, the wording is not. Not a fuel cost: with light unlimited, spending the charge would strand a player lightless for the rest of the run.
charge._rechargeProposal: PROPOSAL, default off, Chris's call: refill the lantern when you bank at the relay. It would make the relay do double duty - securing loot and buying more light - which strengthens the bank-or-push decision. It also softens the charge economy, so it is off until Chris says otherwise.

knockdown._note: Enemies knock Lightkeepers down rather than killing them. A downed player keeps their loot until the crew wipes.
knockdown._dropsCarriedCrateNote: Chris's call, 2026-10-20: a downed Lightkeeper keeps the crate, matching the note above - you keep your loot until the crew wipes. Was true, which did nothing useful: the flag only cleared the carry slot, so the crate still extracted at full value. If this is ever set back to true, RunStateService.knockDown must also remove RestorationCrates from state.haul.carried, or the drop is cosmetic again.
knockdown._bleedOutNote: 0 = downed players wait indefinitely. The handoff's forgiving tone argues against a bleed-out timer in v1; the wipe already comes from the whole crew going down. Set a value only if playtests show downs are being ignored.

revive._note: Server-validated hold. Moving out of range cancels it, so reviving is a real commitment of a teammate's attention - that is the co-op role the handoff asks for.

sweeperContact._note: Day 4 behaviour: a Sweeper that reaches a Lightkeeper knocks them down. Weak alone, dangerous as a swarm.
sweeperContact._hitsNote: hitsToKnockDown with decay is what makes one Sweeper survivable and four lethal, without giving players a health bar to optimise.

movement._note: Movement is a readability and route-choice tool, not a stamina minigame. Sprint gets you to an exit or away from a Sweeper; crouch gives players a deliberate slow mode for tight shops and careful approach. Neither changes Storm Charge.
